tagline: A leading provider of specialty contracting services focused on the digital infrastructure, telecommunications and utilities industries throughout the United States.
hero_kpi_rationale: The Communications segment represents the majority of business operations and is directly linked to the wave of fiber deployment and infrastructure for cloud and AI, making it the primary growth driver.

kpis.name: Communications segment revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue generated by construction, maintenance and installation services in telecommunications and digital infrastructure.
kpis.description: This segment includes fiber placement, wireless networks and engineering services for telecom operators.
kpis.signal: Sustained growth driven by fiber and data centers.

kpis.name: Building Systems segment revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue from infrastructure solutions for data centers, including electrical and security systems.
kpis.description: This segment was strengthened by the acquisition of Power Solutions in 2026, targeting critical infrastructure for data centers. Power Solutions was acquired for $1.95 billion.
kpis.signal: Rapid growth following Power Solutions acquisition.

kpis.name: Gross margin
kpis.explanation: Difference between revenue and cost of services, expressed as a percentage.
kpis.description: Gross margin improves through better management of labor and equipment costs.

kpis.name: Operating margin
kpis.explanation: Operating profit divided by total revenue.
kpis.description: Operating margin advances with scale and cost rationalization.

kpis.name: R&D investments (% of revenue)
kpis.explanation: Research and development spending relative to revenue.
kpis.description: R&D investments are minimal, as the business relies on service execution rather than product innovation.
kpis.signal: Limited R&D, consistent with a services model.

kpis.name: Capital expenditures
kpis.explanation: Annual spending on equipment and tools for operations.
kpis.description: Investments primarily concern vehicles, tools and job site equipment.
kpis.signal: Rising CAPEX to support growth in projects.

kpis.name: Total headcount
kpis.explanation: Total number of employees in the company.
kpis.description: Headcount increases with geographic expansion and new contracts.

kpis.name: Net income
kpis.description: Net income extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL over the last eight reported fiscal years (10-K).
kpis.signal: Net income of $0.281 billion in most recent fiscal year (FY2026).

kpis.name: AT&T revenue share
kpis.explanation: Percentage of revenue generated from AT&T.
kpis.description: AT&T revenue share increased significantly following AT&T's acquisition of Lumen's fiber operations in February 2026. This growth is documented in fiscal 2026 10-K.
kpis.signal: Increased concentration with key customer following fiber acquisition.

kpis.name: Verizon revenue share
kpis.explanation: Percentage of revenue generated from Verizon.
kpis.description: Verizon now includes revenues from Frontier, acquired in January 2026. This combination is reported retrospectively for all presented periods.
kpis.signal: Stable growth related to Frontier Communications integration.

risks.title: Customer concentration
risks.score_rationale: The company is heavily dependent on a few major customers. The four largest customers (AT&T 25.4%, Verizon 14.0%, Lumen 10.8%, Comcast 7.4%) represent 57.6% of total revenues, which constitutes significant risk in case of order reduction or cancellation.

risks.title: Weather and operational risks
risks.score_rationale: Adverse weather conditions may impact the company's operations. The MD&A emphasizes that the cyclical nature of served industries and seasonal conditions affect contract revenues, particularly for outdoor work in the Communications segment.

risks.title: Regulatory risks
risks.score_rationale: Changes in government regulations may affect the company's operations. The MD&A mentions the impact of government policy changes and regulations on customer capital budgets.

risks.title: Competition risks
risks.score_rationale: The company operates in a competitive marketplace. The MD&A indicates that the majority of multi-year contracts are awarded through competitive bids, exposing Dycom to potential market share loss.

risks.title: Acquisition integration risks
risks.score_rationale: The major $1.95 billion Power Solutions acquisition in Q4 fiscal 2026 presents significant integration risks. The transaction includes potential post-closing price adjustments and creation of a new reportable segment.

ai_positioning.summary: Although Dycom does not explicitly mention artificial intelligence as a primary topic, the strategic context indicates indirect exposure through growing demand for cloud and data center infrastructure. The MD&A cites AI deployments and cloud computing as key drivers of digital infrastructure investments.
evidence: MD&A: Demand for high-speed and low-latency connectivity is expanding, driven by data-intensive applications and mobile usage, necessitating extensive wireline network upgrades and extensions, new and expanding fiber and electrical infrastructure for data centers to meet the current and future needs of cloud compute, AI and advanced wireless network deployments.
